tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the espresso gear this site tracks. `products` have a live Amazon price and, when at a genuine low, a BUY call computed from their own price history; otherwise no call. Filter by slot (the role a product plays in a setup), free-text words (brand and model names, partial words and small typos

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Full detail for one product by slug: community sentiment, reference price and basis, date of the latest price observation, portafilter size (machines) or accessory size (sized accessories), superautomatic / manual-lever / hand-grinder flags, product URL and Amazon link. A known product with no price

tools.name: list_slots
tools.description: The slots an espresso setup is built from (machine, grinder, scale, tamper…), with what each is for. Use the ids as search_catalog's `slot`.

tools.name: watch_price
tools.description: Email the user when a product is at a good price (a verified low), or at or under a target price they name. Use after search_catalog/get_product when the user wants to be told when to buy. Ask the user for their email; never invent or reuse one. One watch per email per product; calling again updates

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_catalog, get_product, watch_price · Public sink: watch_price.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_catalog, get_product, watch_price · Public sink: watch_price

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_catalog" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
